Done. Both parts of the report are addressed on branch `fix/retry-file-uploads` (changes uncommitted; let me know if you want commits).

## Root cause

`http.NewRequest` only attaches a replayable `GetBody` for a handful of known readers (`bytes.Buffer`, `bytes.Reader`, `strings.Reader`, `os.File`). A caller-built multipart body is an arbitrary single-use reader, so `retryTransport` set `canReplayBody=false` and, on a 429, `shouldRetry` returned false — uploads failed immediately instead of retrying, while all other calls (whose bodies are already replayable) retried fine.

## Changes

**Fix (`fix(retry)`):** `pipedrive/retry.go`
- `retryTransport.RoundTrip` now buffers non-replayable request bodies up front (when retries are enabled) via a new `bufferRequestBody` helper, rewiring `Body`/`GetBody`/`ContentLength` so they can be replayed. This is a general fix — any arbitrary-reader body now retries on 429/5xx.
- `pipedrive/retry_test.go`: added `TestRetryTransport_RetriesNonReplayableBodyOn429` (failed before, passes now). The existing `TestRetryTransport_DoesNotRetryWhenBodyNotReplayable` still passes (POST + 502 + `RetryAllMethods:false` is intentionally not retried).

**Feature (`feat(files)`):** `pipedrive/v1/files.go`
- Added `Files.AddFile(ctx, fileName, content io.Reader, opts...)` — builds the multipart body for you (like `CallLogs.AddRecording`), using the internal `multipartbody` helper which yields a replayable `*bytes.Reader`, so retries work out of the box.
- Added association options: `WithFilesDealID`, `WithFilesPersonID`, `WithFilesOrgID`, `WithFilesProductID`, `WithFilesActivityID`, `WithFilesLeadID`, `WithFilesProjectID`.
- `internal/multipartbody/multipartbody.go`: added `NewFileWithFields` (file + optional form fields).

## Testing performed
- `go test ./...` — all packages pass.
- `go vet ./...` — clean.
- `gofmt -l` — clean.
- New tests: retry-replays-nonreplayable-body; `AddFile` (basic, association fields, validation); `NewFileWithFields` (fields, replayability, validation).

## Migration notes
- No breaking changes. `Files.Add` (pre-encoded body) is unchanged. `AddFile` is a new additive method.
- Note: with retries enabled, non-replayable request bodies are now buffered into memory so they can be retried — consistent with the SDK's existing multipart behavior, but worth knowing for very large streaming uploads.
